figure: Figure 10.1, caption (Panel B / 'GPU counts and layer ranges schematic' clause)
issue: Caption states 'the canonical host is 8×H100 and the canonical 70B has 8 layers'. A 70B model with 8 layers is impossible under the book's own canonical KV figure, and the figure itself draws 24 layers (1–8, 9–16, 17–24), not 8.
evidence: Independent rederivation from the book's own canonical: FP16 full-MHA KV = 2.62 MB/token = n_layers × 4 × hidden bytes. With hidden = 8192: 2.62e6 / (4 × 8192) = 79.95 ≈ 80 layers. An 8-layer reading would require hidden ≈ 81,875, which no architecture has. Standard 70B (Llama-2-70B class, hidden 8192) has 80 layers. The drawn ranges (1–24 across three GPUs) also contradict '8 layers' even allowing for the 'schematic' disclaimer, which covers GPU counts and ranges, not the layer-count claim itself. Most likely a dropped zero (8 → 80).
root_cause: Typo in Fig 10.1 caption layer count; possibly propagated if the canonical model definition elsewhere repeats it.
correction: Change caption to 'the canonical 70B has 80 layers' (or whatever the canonical model definition in Ch 2/3 states), keeping the 'GPU counts and layer ranges schematic' disclaimer.
acceptance_test: Caption layer count equals the canonical model's layer count used for all KV and pipeline arithmetic elsewhere in the book; grep all occurrences of '8 layers' vs '80 layers' for the canonical 70B. If any other location also says 8 layers, escalate to P0 and fix all anchors.

issue: The PP row's 'Replicates' cell reads 'hidden states', but hidden states are exactly what the same row's 'Communicates' column, the adjacent prose, and Fig 10.1 all treat as *transferred* point-to-point at stage boundaries — not replicated. Listing the same object as both replicated and communicated is either wrong or undefined.
evidence: Same table row: Communicates = 'hidden states → P2P (stage boundaries only)'. Same page prose: 'hidden states cross stage boundaries point-to-point'. Fig 10.1 panel B label: 'activations → P2P at stage boundaries'. Fig 10.1 caption: replication is described 'where it exists (TP's activations in the text; DP's whole model in the panel)' — no PP replication is claimed. Benign-interpretation challenge: the only defensible reading is 'hidden states remain unsharded (full tensors)', but the column header is literally 'Replicates', which conventionally means multiple copies; each stage holds a *different* tensor (layer-8 output vs layer-16 output), so nothing is copied.
root_cause: Column cell conflates 'not partitioned' with 'replicated', or duplicates the Communicates content.
correction: Replace the cell with what PP actually replicates (e.g., '— (full hidden state passes through unsharded)' or 'nothing' with a one-line footnote defining the column), or redefine the column header so 'replicates' ≠ 'transfers'. Table, Fig 10.1, and prose must then agree.
acceptance_test: For each of the five rows, the 'Replicates' cell names an object that exists in multiple copies on multiple devices and does not also appear in that row's 'Communicates' cell unless the duplication is explicitly explained; Fig 10.1 caption's 'replication is described where it exists' list remains accurate.

issue: In the rendered page, all four blue 'sequence in flight' segments appear to terminate at the same x-position, with the pink idle region beginning at that same x in every row. If the blues are uniform, no sequence finishes early, the batch's 'slowest member' is all four simultaneously, and the depicted trailing idle has no cause — contradicting the figure's own labels.
evidence: Caption: 'a batch is locked until its slowest member finishes, so short outputs idle in the trailing slots'. In-figure label: 'GPU slots idle (pink) when a sequence finishes early'. Both require visibly different sequence lengths; the slowest row should show no (or negligible) pink. Rendered inspection at 150 dpi shows four equal-width blues and four pink regions starting at the same x; the 'idle (bubble)' arrow points into row 3's pink as if it were early-finish idle. Confidence is limited by render resolution — this must be checked against the figure source.
root_cause: Either the drawn row lengths are actually equal (semantic error: idle depicted without differential finish times), or differences are too small to read at print size (visual error: the mechanism is invisible).
correction: Make the four blue segments end at clearly different x-positions, with the longest (slowest) row's blue extending to the batch end and little or no pink, so the pink width per row visibly equals that row's early-finish margin.
acceptance_test: At print size, a reader can see at least three distinct blue-end positions; the slowest row shows no pink; pink width per row is proportional to how much earlier that sequence finished; the 'finishes early' label points at a row that is visibly shorter than the slowest row.

figure: Figure 11.3, red aggregate-KV caveat spanning panels A and B
issue: The single caveat spans both panels, but the aggregate check has sharply opposite consequences for the two cases, and the figure never says which case the aggregate actually breaks: on-node decode-side ingress is 4 × 450 = 1.8 TB/s vs 1.4 TB/s payload (feasible when spread, ~78–80% link utilization), while the cross-host path is 40 GB/s vs 1.4 TB/s (infeasible by ~35×). Every clause of the caveat is literally true, but the figure's entire purpose is to contrast A and B, and the caveat flattens that contrast.
evidence: Caveat text: '35 GB/request × 40 req/s = 1.4 TB/s of payload. Per-request times assume an unshared per-GPU link; 1.4 TB/s exceeds any single link above.' Arithmetic verified: 35 × 40 = 1400 GB/s ✓; 35/450 = 0.078 ≈ 0.08 s ✓; 35/40 = 0.875 ≈ 0.9 s ✓. Per-case check: A — 40 rps over 4 GPU pairs = 10 rps/pair × 0.08 s = 0.8 s/s ≈ 80% of one 450 GB/s link (feasible, tight, assumes even spread and TP-sharded KV); B — 40 rps × 0.9 s = 36 link-seconds/s needed vs 1 available ≈ 36× overcommit (infeasible). Note 11.3-1 (PDF 210 / printed 190) likewise stops at 'against the shared fabric' without the per-case aggregate arithmetic, so the reader gets no worked contrast anywhere.
root_cause: One caveat written for two regimes whose aggregate feasibility differs by ~45×; per-case aggregate never derived.
correction: Extend the caveat (or Note 11.3-1) with the per-case aggregate: 'A: 4 decode GPUs × 450 GB/s = 1.8 TB/s ingress can absorb 1.4 TB/s when spread (~80% per-link at 40 rps — feasible but tight); B: 40 GB/s NIC cannot (≈35× over) — so the transfer link, not topology alone, decides whether P/D disaggregation pays,' which also matches the chapter's own 'evaluate against measured phase conflict, not topology alone' guidance.
acceptance_test: The figure or Note 11.3-1 states the aggregate feasibility separately for case A and case B with the arithmetic (capacity vs 1.4 TB/s), and a reader cannot conclude that the on-node case fails at the canonical 40 rps peak.
